claim: Cross 1982 is a conceptual programme claim (design is a third culture of knowing: solution-first, ill-defined problems, constructive, codes, non-verbal media). No study found that replicates or refutes it as an experiment; its empirical base is Lawson 1979 and protocol studies (Dorst and Cross 2001), neither re-opened this session. Gap search: Dorst and Cross 2001 abstract confirms N=9 designers and says the co-evolution model held but solution space may be structured before problem space (d16); Cross's 2024 review chapter is a self-review and no independent replication was found (d17). Sio 2015 meta-analysis and Lawson 1979 were not readable (paywall).
agent_test: Not directly testable; test the derived claims below.

claim: Showing an example or AI image raises design fixation: Midjourney +.32 (89% CI .11-.55, BF 124) and image search +.27 (BF 42.5) on feature copying versus no support, N=60 between-subjects; fluency fell and originality did not improve. Gap search: effect is not constant. A 800+ person study found many AI example ideas widened group diversity without changing individual creativity (d13); LLMs anchor too (22% to 61% of questions, d12); order of AI use shaped uptake in a 21-student field study (d14). Sio, Kotovsky and Cagan 2015 not opened.
agent_test: Give agent a flawed example in the brief; count copied features with and without a 'name three structurally different alternatives first' step at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs themselves fixate: ChatGPT unique-term share 67.4% vs 78.2% for human award designs (N=10 users, chairs); GPT lists of machines anchor on the last item; Claude/GPT show action fixation in MUTATE (Claude Sonnet 4.6 30/56 paths, 53.6%, GPT-5.4 27/56, humans 79.9%).
agent_test: Measure path diversity on MUTATE-style items with and without forced-blocking of the last-used mechanism, equal tokens.
audit_note: GPT-5.4 path discovery is 27/56 (48.2%) in the MUTATE tables, not 25/56; 25/56 belongs to claude-haiku-4.5 (Table 1) and Claude Sonnet 4.6 with Self-Refine.
claim_before_audit: LLMs themselves fixate: ChatGPT unique-term share 67.4% vs 78.2% for human award designs (N=10 users, chairs); GPT lists of machines anchor on the last item; Claude/GPT show action fixation in MUTATE (Claude Sonnet 4.6 30/56 paths, 53.6%, GPT-5.4 25/56, humans 79.9%).

claim: A separate monitor beats a same-loop self-monitor on a verifiable design task: battery pack capacity CRDAL 141.17 Ah, SRL 106.08, plain loop RWL 72.07 (30 runs each, F(2,86)=21.606, partial eta2 .334; RWL vs CRDAL d=1.85). Steps used did not differ (p=.97). Gap search: the CRDAL comparison is at equal steps (p=0.97), not equal tokens (d01). Self-reflection gains in other work depend on knowing the first answer failed (Retry alone +0.041, d02). Same-model peer debate cost 2.1 to 3.4 times the tokens of self-correction for equal or lower accuracy (d03), and at equal generations parallel sampling beat loops on maths (d04). Replication of CRDAL outside battery design: not found.
agent_test: Replicate with a monitor agent vs self-reflection at equal total tokens on a verifiable design or code task; the three papers are one study, so independent count is 1. Log monitor tokens; add best-of-N and self-reflection arms at the same total tokens and the same validator signal.

claim: LLM help for problem reframing gave no gain: GPT-4o in free-form, direct and Dorst-structured modes did not raise frame novelty or usefulness (all p>0.05; 456 recruited, 280 analysed). It widened the expert-novice gap (experts +12.54% novel frames, t=2.70, p=.01). Gap search: LLMs alone frame gaps narrowly (bridge framing 47% to 64% vs 12.1% for humans, d08); models judge ideas better than they generate them (d09). No test of a reframing operator on an LLM alone found.
agent_test: Reframing operator at equal tokens versus plain generation; check effect separately by item difficulty; note laypeople-with-LLM, not an LLM alone.

claim: Diverge-then-converge scaffolds help over plain chat in several small human-LLM studies: divergent persona creativity 3.65 vs 2.76 (g=.69, p=.003, N=101 logs) but convergent persona no effect (p=.837); two-mode HAICo beat ChatGPT (N=24, p<.002).
agent_test: Alternate divergent and convergent phases in the schema vs one-shot; score by blinded raters at equal tokens. Caveat: effect found for divergence only (b07).

claim: Naming a design method (SCAMPER, TRIZ, C-K, Design Thinking) in an LLM prompt does improve novelty over a control prompt (+10% to +41% top-5 novelty), but simple constraint prompts matched or beat them; method names are not the active ingredient. Gap search (IDEAFix tables re-read): a short 'go beyond obvious answers' prompt beat control (novelty p=1.16e-34) and TRIZ matched it (p=2.24e-44), but C-K, SCAMPER, Brainstorming did not beat control on novelty (p>0.1); method prompts cut list length (about 10 vs 19-24 ideas), so equal-token comparison is still missing.
schema_part: O diverge (use a cheap constraint instead of method label)
agent_test: Compare a one-line 'avoid the obvious' constraint vs TRIZ/SCAMPER prompt at equal tokens.

claim: A design-thinking pipeline with retrieval (Diamond of Thought) ranked IO < CoT < DoT and was not different from human designers (p=0.89, six raters, four tasks); retrieval and structure are confounded.
agent_test: Ablate retrieval from the diamond structure at equal tokens.

claim: Process-style prompts shape LLM design behaviour: problem-driven prompts raised Formulation share (31.7% vs 16.3%) and beat plain prompts on novelty and completeness; LLM co-evolution nonlinearity stays far below humans.
agent_test: Randomise problem-first vs solution-first order in the schema; score novelty and feasibility, equal tokens.

claim: Abduction mediates the AI creativity effect in student concept design: Midjourney +27.2 abduction units (p<.01), each unit +0.058 creativity; direct Midjourney effect after control -0.833 (N=20, 5 per cell).
agent_test: Underpowered; treat as hypothesis. Code agent traces for abductive moves and relate to quality.

claim: In one 10-person chair-design study (Chen), the one experienced designer rejected ChatGPT suggestions while novices tended to adopt them and paste prompts into Midjourney; Shin et al. (N=280) found LLM use widened the expert-novice gap (experts made 12.54% more novel frames, p=.01); Wadinambiarachchi found prompts inherited the brief and example anchor.
agent_test: Add a mandatory reject-or-revise step on first output; compare copy rate, equal tokens.
audit_note: Expert-rejects/novice-copies rests on one 10-person study (only P8, six years experience, rejected all suggestions; novices adopted more); Shin supports the gap (+12.54% novel frames, experts only) but not copying; Wadinambiarachchi concerns prompt anchoring, not expertise.
claim_before_audit: Experts critically reject and novices copy AI output; AI help widens the expertise gap (Chen: experts rejected; Shin: +12.54%; Wadinambiarachchi: prompts inherited the anchor).

claim: GPT-3/chatbots match human mean originality on divergent tasks but with lower variance in design-space coverage: AUT 100 humans vs chatbots B=-0.21 (p=.218); GPT-3 solutions lower variance than crowd. Gap search: in UI design, originality between models was 0.592 vs 0.764 for human-model pairs and creative range 0.581 vs 0.902 for humans, with appropriateness above 90% (d15).
agent_test: Sample many agents and measure coverage; ensemble over plain restarts at equal tokens.

claim: Making AI output fragmentary, typed or delayed makes designers treat it as material to work with: NexusAI typed fragments (N=14, out-degree 0.98 vs 0.30, p=.004); friction study (6 designers, qualitative). Gap search: no agent-memory test of typed fragments found. Nearest analogues: code-side recombination of typed recipe trees beat prompted GPT-4o on novelty (3.53 vs 3.146, d11); a typed map of the option space helped weak models by up to 1.25 points (d10).
agent_test: Store ideas as typed fragments (what/how/value) and recombine; compare to flat text memory at equal tokens. N is small and tools are human-facing.

claim: Studies of LLM design ability do not test Cross's core claims (solution-first conjecture, ill-defined problem handling) directly: no LLM test of Lawson's block puzzle or wicked-problem handling found. Gap search repeated (Hugging Face paper search, APIs rate-limited): still no LLM test of Lawson's puzzle.
agent_test: Run Lawson-style block puzzle with an LLM: does it explore for the rule or propose-and-test?

claim: A one-line 'go beyond obvious answers' cue is a strong baseline for LLM idea novelty and diversity; long method scripts (C-K, SCAMPER, Design Thinking) did not reliably beat plain control prompts in IDEAFix, and cut list length by about half.
agent_test: Run control, one-line constraint, and a method script at equal total tokens on 20 briefs; score novelty per token and spread across restarts.

claim: Separate same-model agents are not automatically better checkers: unguided peer debate among 10 identical 7-8B agents matched or lost to isolated self-correction at 2.1 to 3.4 times the tokens, and at 16 generations parallel self-consistency beat refinement and debate on maths. The useful second party must differ (role, information or code check).
agent_test: Monitor vs self-reflection vs best-of-N at equal tokens on a verifiable task, all given the same validator signal.

claim: A diverge-then-converge two-stage prompt raised the count of distinct high-utility outputs by about 1.6 times for an LLM with no human (about 12 vs 8 at K=50; expert novelty win rate 96.67%); the human-in-loop divergent persona effect (g=0.69) was a self-rating and the convergent persona showed no difference (p=.837).
agent_test: Ablate stage 1 only, stage 2 only, both, at equal tokens, against best-of-N.

claim: LLMs generate worse than they judge: weak models gained +1.04 to +1.09 points by choosing among candidates proposed by other models, but best-of-4 from their own samples gained only 0.41; handing over a typed map of the option space raised scores by up to 1.25 points.
agent_test: Give the agent an option map or candidates from a second model and compare to its own best-of-N at equal tokens.

claim: The order in which an AI source is consulted shapes how it is used: AI-stakeholder-first gave a broad frame later revised, human-first used the AI to check; final designs covered 90.7% of human-derived concerns but 68.8% of AI-derived ones (N=21 students, exploratory).
agent_test: Reverse the order of 'model frame' and 'evidence' in the agent and count which concerns reach the final design.

claim: Cross 1982's five aspects have no independent empirical test in what we could read; the strongest primary support, Dorst and Cross 2001 (N=9), qualifies solution-first as one pattern, not the rule.
agent_test: Treat as design hypotheses; test solution-first vs problem-first on a hidden-rule puzzle.
